outcome: No case or variant of the Grand Riemann Hypothesis (the critical-line claim for all automorphic L-functions) has been settled since 26 January 2024; only unconditional zero-free-region and zero-density work on automorphic L-functions, and a major AI-assisted result confined to the classical Riemann zeta function alone, were found.
summary: The Grand Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) as stated on this bullet — that the nontrivial zeros of ALL automorphic L-functions lie on the critical line — remains completely open, with no case or genuine variant settled since 26 January 2024. Ordinary literature progress continues: an unconditional 'Explicit zero-free regions for automorphic L-functions' (arXiv 2509.20873, submitted 26 Sept 2025) improves classical-style zero-free-region bounds for this L-function class but explicitly does not touch the critical-line assertion (per my own reading of the paper, confirmed via WebFetch) — this is progress on a companion unconditional question, not a restriction of GRH itself, so it does not even count as 'progress' on the stated bullet under the scope rule (§3.1), since the bullet is an existence/universal claim that only moves if some case is fully settled. A 2024 preprint on low-lying zero density for a large automorphic family (arXiv 2408.09050) is likewise a statistical/density result assuming GRH, not a step toward proving it. The most substantively interesting nearby event is Anthropic's August 2026 announcement that an unreleased research version of Claude discovered a proof raising the known lower bound on the proportion of zeros of the classical Riemann zeta function ζ(s) that are simple and/or on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2% (published as Alpöge & Furman, 'More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line,' arXiv 2608.13637, verified by Anthropic mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman). This is a real, well-documented, human-verified AI mathematical result (arguably 'generated' under §6.2, since the authors' own account states the argument was discovered and written by Claude and the named authors verified and take responsibility for it) — but it concerns only ζ(s), the single simplest automorphic L-function (GL(1) over Q), not 'all automorphic L-functions' as the bullet requires, and even for ζ(s) it is a percentage/density bound, not a settlement of any case (the bullet is a universal claim that only moves when fully answered, per §3.1's rule on existence/infinitude-type questions — a density bound on a single L-function narrows nothing about the universal claim across the whole automorphic family). Because classical RH (the ζ(s) case) has its own separate Wikipedia bullet distinct from this one, and this result does not purport to say anything about non-trivial automorphic L-functions (GL(2) and higher, or L-functions of general automorphic representations), I classify it as a related/neighbouring result rather than a case of this stated problem, and note the classification is a close call given ζ(s) is technically a (degenerate) automorphic L-function. The fringe 'Unified Proof of the Extended, Generalized, and Grand Riemann Hypothesis' preprint (posted to preprints.org and ResearchGate, October 2025 through an April 2026 v14 revision) is an unrefereed, non-peer-reviewed claim with no expert digestion, no journal acceptance, and no corroborating commentary found anywhere (Tao's blog, MathOverflow, or specialist number-theory venues); it sits alongside a long-standing genre of perennial unrefereed RH-family 'proof' claims and does not change the status. Terence Tao's blog in 2026 mentions GRH only in passing as background for the Langlands program, with no technical claim of progress. No AI system, LLM, or machine-learning approach was found targeting the automorphic-L-function generalization itself (searches for ML/AI work on automorphic or higher-degree L-function zeros turned up only a LightGBM classifier predicting Dirichlet-character conductors from statistical zero features — an empirical pattern-detection exercise, not a proof-relevant result, and unrelated to the critical-line question).
competing_reading: One could argue the Alpöge–Furman/Claude zeta result should be recorded as `partial` progress on GRH with `ai_role: generated`, since ζ(s) is literally an automorphic L-function (the L-function of the trivial automorphic representation of GL(1)) and a density bound narrows what could still be false. Two things weigh against this: (1) classical RH already has its own dedicated Wikipedia bullet, so treating any RH-only result as also moving the GRH bullet would double-count the same event across two records; (2) per §3.1's explicit rule, GRH is stated as a universal/existence-type claim ('do the zeros... lie on the line') that 'moves only when it is answered' — a percentage bound on one instance out of the full automorphic family is precisely the kind of density/record result the rule says does not count, even setting aside the double-counting concern. If a future auditor disagrees with either premise, the correct status would become `progress` with `ai_role: generated` and the systems/sources fields populated from the Anthropic page and arXiv 2608.13637.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the classical-RH-only Anthropic/Claude zeta-zero bound should be attributed to this GRH bullet at all, given classical RH's separate bullet on the same list — a documented editorial decision on how the two bullets' scopes are meant to be kept disjoint would settle it either way.
